## objectui#6356 — measurement first, then a stop: `needs_decision`

`domain:ui` seat #1 dispatch, dev run `session_01DuWo5bdP9SdVebamn99GGk` (`mode:subagent`). Read at objectui `bff63cc12` (branch base) and objectstack `0d3ec471`. No PR: nothing was narrowed, per the claim's stop line. Three choices remain that change what an author may write, so they go to the seat as `open_questions`. The measurement below is the deliverable. Generics and placeholders are spelled in words on purpose, because GitHub strips tag-shaped text from bodies.

### What the card says, checked against `main`

- The card says "`items` is declared `any[]`". That is **stale**. objectui#7164 and objectui#7365 have since declared both levels, on both halves, as OBJECTS whose keys stay open (`.passthrough()` in the mirror, a string index signature in the TS type). The element's own keys are still undeclared, so the card's core still holds: `{ title, date }` type-checks and parses green (Table 3).
- The card says there are "two element shapes". There are really **three read sets**. `horizontal` drops five keys that `vertical` reads (Table 2), so the card's feed row in its table is the vertical read set, not a shared one.
- The card says `meta` / `group` come from `ObjectTimeline` and are read by `TimelineRenderer`. **Confirmed**, and they are read by the vertical branch only.
- **New fact.** The strict authoring face (objectui#8345, `deriveStrictAuthoringSchema`) refuses **every legitimate timeline element** today, including the schema-catalog's own feed items and gantt rows and bars (Table 3). The element and the bar declare no keys, so the face closes them to nothing. The objectui#5250 ruling says `objectui validate` and the doc-snippet gates will run strict. Declaring the element is therefore a prerequisite for wiring that face without false refusals.
- Zone 2 assumption 1 (file locations) holds. Assumption 2 holds too: PR objectui#10714's 18 file patches mention `Timeline` zero times in `data-display.ts` and `data-display.zod.ts`, so the two changes touch separate regions.

### Instrument

- **Static walk.** A TypeScript-AST walk plus a JSON walk over `git ls-files`, on a clean worktree (so every file read is the HEAD blob). In objectui it covered 8785 files with 0 parse failures. Fenced code blocks in `.md` and `.mdx` files were parsed too.
- **What counts as a timeline node.** An object literal whose `type` is `timeline`, `plugin-timeline:timeline`, `object-timeline` or `view:timeline`. For registration examples and render props, the walk also counts an object whose `variant` is vertical, horizontal or gantt and that carries `items`.
- **Lit control.** A synthetic two-file repo authors `meta`, `group`, `color`, `startDate`, `endDate`, `_data` and `date`, once in an `apps/` TS file and once in a `skills/` JSON fence. The walk reported every one of those keys.
- **Render probes.** A throwaway vitest file rendered the real `TimelineRenderer`. It was deleted uncommitted, and the tree was verified clean with `git status --porcelain` = 0.
- **Strict-face probe.** `tsx` ran against `packages/types/src`.
- **Not re-derivable from this comment alone.** The scripts lived in the session scratchpad. The follow-up implementation should re-take Table 1 with a committed instrument if it wants a gate.

### Table 1 — element keys authored in each corpus

The figure after each key is the number of elements that carry it.

| corpus (files) | feed elements | feed keys | gantt rows / bars | row keys / bar keys |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| schema-catalog JSON (3) | 8 | time 8, title 8, description 8, variant 8, icon 4 | 3 / 5 | label 3, items 3 / title, startDate, endDate, variant: 5 each |
| docs `plugin-timeline.mdx` (1) | 10 | time 10, title 10, variant 10, description 9, icon 7 | 2 / 3 | label 2, items 2 / 3 each |
| package md: `TIMELINE.md`, plugin-timeline `README.md` (2) | 11 | time 11, title 11, variant 10, description 9, icon 4, className 1, content 1 | 3 / 9 | label 3, items 3 / 9 each |
| registration `defaultProps` plus `examples` (`plugin-timeline:timeline`) | 10 | time 10, title 10, description 10, variant 10, icon 4 | 3 / 5 | label 3, items 3 / 5 each |
| `apps/` (298 files), `skills/` (27 files) | **0** | none | 0 | none |
| objectstack, whole tree (9418 files; 21 timeline-typed nodes: 2 list views, 1 component-manifest entry in `sdui.manifest.json`, 18 in tests) | **0** outside tests | none | 0 | none |
| test fixtures (15 files; they show which tests a narrowing would reach, not what authors write) | 15 | title 15, time 13, description 6, variant 3, **date 2** | 7 / 7 | label 7, items 7 / title, startDate, endDate: 7 |

- **Authored totals** (the four authoring corpora combined):
  - Feed: 39 elements. time 39, title 39, variant 38, description 36, icon 19, className 1, content 1.
  - Feed keys never authored: `color`, `meta`, `group`, `startDate` and `endDate` all score **0**.
  - Gantt: 11 rows, all carrying `label` and `items`. 22 bars, all carrying `title`, `startDate`, `endDate` and `variant`.
- **The seven feed keys agree everywhere.** The authored feed vocabulary is exactly the seven keys the docs page documents. The registration's `inputs` description lists six of them and omits `className`.
- **Authored `variant` values** on elements and bars are default 6, success 25, info 16, warning 12, danger 3: exactly the documented five. The marker also paints `todo`, `in-progress` and `done` (zero authored); the bar paints only the five. Lit control: the same grep hits the node-level values vertical 11, horizontal 4, gantt 5.
- **Test fixtures.** `ObjectTimeline.test.tsx` authors `{ title, date }` twice, typed `schema: any`. `date` is the `TimelineEvent` vocabulary and nothing reads it off an item, so the two tests assert the title only. This is the card's trap, live in-repo.

### Table 2 — what each feed branch reads, measured in render

The probe rendered one item carrying every candidate key, with `dateFormat: 'iso'`.

| key | vertical | horizontal |
|---|---|---|
| time, title, description, icon, className | drawn | drawn |
| color (marker style) | drawn | **dropped** |
| meta (chips) | drawn | **dropped** |
| group (sticky bucket header) | drawn | **dropped** |
| startDate (as the only date), endDate | drawn | **dropped** |
| date | dropped | dropped |

- **Not re-probed.** `variant` and `content` are read by both branches in source (the `TimelineMarker` variant and `renderChildren(item.content)`).
- **Gantt read set.** The gantt branch reads row `label` / `items` and bar `title` / `startDate` / `endDate` / `variant`. The existing gantt suites pin that, so it was not re-probed.
- **The only producer of the five composed-only keys** is `ObjectTimeline`'s `effectiveItems` memo, which composes `{ title, time, startDate, endDate, description, variant, color, group, meta, _data }` per record. Its click handler reads `_data`. `ListView` and `ObjectView` hand it config and never items.

### Table 3 — what each door answers today

| input | tolerant mirror (`safeValidateSchema`, what `objectui validate` runs) | strict face (objectui#8345, not wired yet) | render |
|---|---|---|---|
| catalog feed item | accept | **refuse**: `unrecognized_keys` at items.0 [time, title, description, variant, icon] | draws |
| catalog gantt row and bar | accept | **refuse**: items.0 [label] and items.0.items.0 [title, startDate, endDate, variant] | draws |
| `{ title, date }` | accept | refuse (both keys, the same way as any key) | title only; date silently dropped |
| a feed item under `variant: 'gantt'` | accept | refuse (every element key) | empty unlabelled row, **no diagnostic** |
| a gantt row under `vertical` / `horizontal` | accept | refuse (every element key) | empty item, **no diagnostic** |

The two cross-shape rows are the evidence for the second question below. A union at the element level accepts both of them by construction, because each is a valid arm.

### Reproduce the cross-shape reading

```ts
// vitest file under packages/plugin-timeline/src/__tests__/, run from the repo root
import React from 'react';
import { render } from '@testing-library/react';
import { TimelineRenderer } from '../renderer';
import { TimelineSchema } from '@object-ui/types/zod';
const feed = { time: '2024-01-15', title: 'FEED_TITLE' };
const row = { label: 'ROW_LABEL', items: [{ title: 'BAR_TITLE', startDate: '2024-01-01', endDate: '2024-02-01' }] };
for (const schema of [
  { type: 'timeline', variant: 'gantt', items: [feed] },
  { type: 'timeline', variant: 'vertical', items: [row] },
]) {
  const ok = TimelineSchema.safeParse(schema).success;            // true, both
  const html = render(React.createElement(TimelineRenderer, { schema })).container.innerHTML;
  // neither FEED_TITLE nor ROW_LABEL nor BAR_TITLE, and no role="alert"
}
```

The same shapes under their own variant are the lit control: `FEED_TITLE` draws under vertical, and `ROW_LABEL` plus `BAR_TITLE` draw under gantt.

## Measurement delivered ⇒ two contract-shape questions to the box · `domain:ui` seat #1 · 2026-09-27T15:55Z

`session_01DuWo5bdP9SdVebamn99GGk` (`os-steve`). The card is measurement-first. The dev measured, wrote nothing (the claim's stop line), and returned three questions (report `5857222802`, which holds the tables). The seat re-read the one reading everything rests on: on objectui `origin/main`, `TimelineSchema.items` is `z.array(TimelineRowSchema)` (`packages/types/src/zod/data-display.zod.ts:1135`), not the body's `any[]`. The element is an object with its keys still open. ⇒ The card's core stands, and its body's framing is stale.

Release: `session_01DuWo5bdP9SdVebamn99GGk` · cause: measurement done, two open contract-shape choices · destination: `needs-user-decision`. The claim `5857054090` is spent. The branch `claude/issue-6356-timeline-item-element` holds no commits beyond base. The next dispatch re-claims.

Governing text: this card's triage block (「`items` … enforces nothing … an AI authoring timeline items meets no refusal」, maintainer-confirmed); triage `5853468236` (the three execution questions, `Clause-②: yes`); objectui#10222 letter A (the same posture for the chip-field list that produces `meta`); the pm-dispatch base principle 「spec 声明 > 实现 > 文档面」.

### One-line problem

An author (human or AI) can put any keys on a timeline item, or put a gantt row on a feed timeline. Both are accepted, and the wrong parts just do not draw. In addition, the strict authoring check that `objectui validate` is due to run would refuse **every** legitimate timeline element today, because the element declares no keys at all (measured, report Table 3).

### Q1 — `meta`, `group`, `color`, `startDate`, `endDate` on a feed item: authorable, or renderer-internal?

| | what it means | cost, measured |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **A** | Renderer-internal. The authored feed element declares the documented seven (`time, title, description, variant, icon, content, className`). The five composed-only keys get an internal type inside `plugin-timeline` for the `ObjectTimeline` → renderer handoff. | Zero authored instances across four authoring corpora, `apps/`, `skills/` and objectstack. Anyone who authors `meta` today would be refused once the strict face is wired. |
| **B** | Authorable, on vertical only. Needs a three-way element split (vertical / horizontal / gantt), because horizontal drops all five. | Five keys declared with zero pull, plus a three-arm discrimination. |
| **C** | Authorable on one shared feed element. | Declares keys that horizontal silently drops (report Table 2) ⇒ not viable. |

### Q2 — one union, or a pair discriminated by the node's `variant`?

| | what it means | cost, measured |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **A** | Element union (feed item or gantt row); `TimelineSchema` stays an interface and a `ZodObject`. | Refuses unknown keys, but NOT a gantt row on a feed timeline (silent today, Table 3). |
| **B** | Split node: TS `TimelineSchema` becomes a union alias and the zod mirror a union. | Refuses cross-shape in TS and in validate. The published zod `TimelineSchema` stops being a `ZodObject` (`.shape` / `.extend` gone; 4 test files and the parity ratchet use them); the tombstones ride on both arms. |
| **C** | TS element union as in A, plus a node-level `superRefine` in the zod mirror that judges each element against the arm `variant` selects (absent ⇒ vertical). This is the house pattern for cross-key rules (`calendarSelectionFitsMode`, `requireRecordSource`). | Refuses unknown keys AND cross-shape at the JSON door AI authors use. TS literals still get excess-key errors; cross-shape is caught at validate, not at compile. Two tests move from `.extend` to `.safeExtend`. |

### 业务含义直译

- **Q1-A**:时间线条目上作者能写的,就是文档写着的那七个;另外五个是组件内部自己拼出来的,不对外承诺。
- **Q1-B / C**:把内部拼装用的键也变成对外承诺;可是没有人在写它们,而且横向布局根本不画。
- **Q2-A**:能拦住乱写的键,拦不住「把甘特行塞进普通时间线」。
- **Q2-B**:编译期也能拦住串用,但要把一个已发布的 schema 拆成两个,测试和一致性检查都得跟着改。
- **Q2-C**:在作者和 AI 真正走的 JSON 校验入口,两种错都响亮拒绝,已发布的形状不动。

### 四轴论证(业务立场)
